interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body:
The postoperative pathology reveals a Gleason 3+3 (ISUP grade group 1) and pathological stage pT2c. A positive surgical margin was documented, which is an adverse finding. Counterbalancing this is the absence of extraprostatic extension and the finding that "the seminal vesicles were not invaded." Lymphovascular invasion was absent. Nodal status is documented as "no lymph nodes were removed," which means pNx does not establish node-negative disease, widening uncertainty regarding nodal involvement.

The prognosis is influenced by the positive margin status. The absence of documented seminal vesicle invasion is reassuring. Postoperative PSA is not recorded, meaning biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its trajectory would significantly revise the prognosis. Missing nodal sampling further limits the certainty of the stage. The fixed estimated horizon is 49.00 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 29.40–68.60 months; its coverage has not been validated.
